title: 54430006-Dead_or_Alive_1_Ultimate.xiso.iso
replaces: tbflip424-blinx.json. Its Thor pilot (1790473035 / 1790473037) could not run: the Thor is under the owner's hold (2026-09-27T02:30Z, charging), and Blinx is staged on the Thor only. That pair is withdrawn without a result. hostops 19:51 PDT asked for M4' on a Nova title instead. Nothing from the Blinx prediction was measured, so nothing here is refit to its data.

arms.A: 231d04df51 (master after PR #434 and 38 later commits; the only accel/ change among them is PR #443's [jc425] probe counters in cpu-exec.c, which both arms carry; HAKUX_TCG68_JC stays unset, so off, in both), no --env: whole-page TB invalidation, the shipped default
arms.B: 231d04df51, the same apk, --env HAKUX_TCG424_RANGE=1: range test plus per-page code bitmap. The env is the only independent variable.

why_this_title: Blinx was the cost-side title: low churn (2-3% of the vCPU thread) and slow stores well above invalidations, so the range test's added per-store cost could outweigh what it saves. Of the Nova titles with a survey soak that reaches play and carries [tlb68] lines, DOA1 Ultimate is closest to that. On titlebench's 1790467161-titlebench-2613663 (d0e30924f8, pre-#434, so A's code path), playread.py reads churn% 1.2, slow/s 1115 against inv/s 305 (3.7x; Blinx 1.4x), and gfps 27.5 against the title's target of 60. It runs below its cap, so a cost can show in gfps. Crimson was not chosen: M3 already priced it (26 -> 29), so it cannot test the cost side. CoD3 (2614040) runs at 29 against a cap of 30, and AUF (2612497) reads churn 0.6.
runs: 54430006-Dead_or_Alive_1_Ultimate.xiso.iso, --route survey (titlebench's DOA1U soak), --seconds 420 (as titlebench), --device nova, 3 runs per arm interleaved A B A B A B. Pilot = the first A and the first B (2 x (420 + 90) s = 17 min).
reader: python3 docs/lanes/tbflip424/playread.py <result ids>, unchanged from its commit 442834864e. Window: `mark play` + 30 s to the end of the log. No mark = VOID. Per run: gfps = the median of the hakuX-perf gfps samples in the window; churn% = (jcus + rdus) / vCPU cpu over the [tlb68] lines in the window. Per arm: the median of its three per-run values. The survey route's span median is NOT read.
why_this_window: The survey route writes `mark play` after 14 START/A rounds (~200 s). On titlebench's DOA1U run every play frame after the mark is a STAGE 01 fight with health bars and a round timer (route-frames/192135-play.png through 192434-play.png). What those frames cannot say is whether the fight is under the pad or the attract demo. Both run the game's fight loop, the thing measured here. The 30 s settle is churn.py's own default, not chosen for this data.
baseline_on_disk: One run, pre-#434 binary (A's path): ng 46, n 78, gfps 27.5, G 37.9 ms, churn% 1.2, di/s 319, slow/s 1115, inv/s 305, tail 0.9 s, fatal 0. It sets the scale only. There is no B-arm baseline on this title.

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run has a `mark play` line, >= 20 gfps samples in the window, [tlb68] in >= 90% of the window's 2 s windows, and xx = 0. A's [tlb68] lines carry rt=0 only; B's carry rt=1 only. A run failing this is VOID, not zero: it is re-queued once on the same arm. More than one VOID run per arm stops the lane without a verdict. FAILS in a world where the route no longer reaches `mark play` on the Nova, perf lines are missing, or the env does not reach the emulator (B shows rt=0).
legs.M1 (the counter moves; the falsifier): Per-arm median churn%: A >= 0.5, and B <= 0.5 x A. Per-arm median di/s: A >= 100 and B <= 0.1 x A. FAILS in a world where DOA1U's fights spend next to nothing on the two #424 mechanisms (A < 0.5% or di/s < 100). Then the arm tests only the added cost, which is still M4''s question, but report it as a cost-only arm. It also fails where the range test does not engage (B's churn or di/s stays near A's); then M4' is inert and does not license the flip. The floor is 0.5, not the Blinx prediction's 1.0, because the one on-disk run reads 1.2, and a floor at 1.0 would decide M1 on noise. Stated before any run.
legs.M4' (must not regress, on gameplay): Per-arm median gfps: B >= A - 1. And no run of either arm crashes: no `Fatal signal` or `FATAL` line in logcat.txt, and the window's last gfps sample is within 15 s of the route's `soak end` line. FAILS in a world where the range test's per-store cost outweighs the churn it removes on a low-churn, store-heavy title (slow/s ~3.7x inv/s). Then B's gameplay median falls more than 1 gfps, about 4% at this title's ~27 gfps.
legs.decision: Flip the default in hakux_tcg424_range_on() iff M0, M1 (both parts) and M4' all pass. If M4' fails, do not flip: diagnose from cb/s, inv/s and slow/s, and report on #424. If M1 fails because A < 0.5 while M4' passes, report the arm as cost-only. The flip still needs the B-side engagement (B <= 0.5 x A on di/s) to count.

what_this_cannot_see: Self-modifying code that a spared block should have caught; the range test makes invalidation do LESS. This arm shows no crash and no fps loss on one title's fight loop on the Nova, not on Blinx. The pgraph must-not-move check on the flipped binary is a separate step, done after the flip.
expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures, so there is no golden key. The legs are read with playread.py off the [tlb68], hakuX-pages and hakuX-perf lines.
